question: Can the Coxeter-length filtration F_l = span{T_w : l(w) <= l} carry the partition grading Z^(k) = span{e_lambda : gbDepth(lambda) = k} that four content blocks read off prop:curvature-rank-gb-stratification?
retraction: This probe retracts my own claim (PR #5205, bean wpdb) that the word-side rank is probably not well defined on the quotient. mba-step07-gb-filtration.md defines the filtration by Coxeter length on S_n, which is well defined by Matsumoto. The objection does not apply.
necessary_condition: #{lambda |- n : gbDepth = k} <= #{w in S_n : l(w) = k} for all k, since the e_lambda are linearly independent and the T_w are a basis
verdict: fails at n = 2 and n = 3; holds for 4 <= n <= 7
why_it_matters: n = 3 is the single-nucleon case -- H_3 is where the framework's m_p / m_n results live. gbDepth is constant (= 3) on all three partitions of 3, so the reading needs dim gr_3 >= 3, but only the longest element of S_3 has length 3, so dim gr_3 = 1.
scope: Scope-(b) where it fails -- a subspace cannot exceed the dimension of its ambient space, so this is a proved exclusion of the charitable reading of the identification, not a failed probe. It is NOT a refutation of the mass results, and other readings of Z^(k) are untouched.
